# Concurrent cap-normal motion and exact global section cancellation

This note separates a valid continuous-normal variation from an invalid mixed ambient rotation, gives explicit cap-decreasing motions for a lone noncanonical simplex group, and checks the full mixed section force in the actual critical star of **candidate 8ac7846221e4d65a**.

The outcomes differ. The lone-simplex variance examples admit a first-order improvement once suitable normal and meeting-point motions are allowed. In the actual centrally symmetric star, the corresponding global forces vanish exactly, despite nonzero endpoint forces and noncanonical thresholds. No stationarity of one fiber is substituted for global cap stationarity.

## 1. The precise cover-preserving normal variations

Fix an affine meeting section
\[
q(z)=Bz+c,\qquad z\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
and a group of closed caps
\[
H_i=\{(z,x):L_i(z,x)\ge0\},\qquad
L_i(z,x)=u_i\cdot(x-q(z)).
\tag{1}
\]
Assume the continuous normals positively span \(\mathbb R^d\), equivalently
\(0\in\operatorname{int}\operatorname{conv}\{u_i\}\).
Then the group covers all of \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\).

Moreover this cover persists under all sufficiently small independent changes of the \(u_i\), provided the margins retain form (1) with one common affine \(q\). Indeed
\[
\rho=\min_{|v|=1}\max_i u_i\cdot v>0.
\]
If \(\max_i|\widetilde u_i-u_i|<\rho\), then
\(\max_i\widetilde u_i\cdot v>0\) for every unit \(v\). At any point off the meeting section apply this with \(v=(x-q(z))/|x-q(z)|\). On the section every margin is zero, so every closed cap contains it. This is a uniform full-space assertion, not a compact-source cover approximation.

For a simplex circuit of \(d+1\) normals, rank \(d\) and a strictly positive dependence imply the stated positive spanning. A single cap may therefore rotate while the others stay fixed. Positive rescaling of a normal does not change its cap, so normalizing the moving normal gives an actual angular motion about the meeting section. The same argument allows \(q\) itself to move, as long as every cap in the group uses the same new section.

**A point alone is insufficient in a mixed space.** In coordinates \((z,x)\), the caps \(x\ge0\) and \(-x\ge0\) cover the plane and meet at \((0,0)\), with strictly balanced continuous normals \(1,-1\). Replace the first by \(x+\varepsilon z\ge0\). Both still pass through \((0,0)\), and the continuous normals have not changed, but the point \((z,x)=(-1,\varepsilon/2)\) lies in neither cap. Thus arbitrary ambient rotations through a common point need not preserve cover. Formula (1) retains the entire common affine section, and changes the base coefficient together with the continuous normal.

The independent motions discussed here refer to separately labeled caps in a group. If one cap is required to be shared by several groups with different meeting sections, its simultaneous restrictions must be retained; independent variation of its multiple occurrences is not automatic.

## 2. Actual mixed cap gradients

Let \(P\) be finite and let each \(K_z\subset\mathbb R^d\) be a full-dimensional compact convex fiber, with the source given by the sum of its \(d\)-volumes. For one cap (1), assume each fiber cut is proper, or else strictly full or strictly empty. Proper means the boundary meets the interior of the fiber. Define the actual coarea section measure
\[
d\tau_z(x)=\frac{1}{|u|}
\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}(x)\big|_{K_z\cap\{u\cdot(x-q(z))=0\}},
\]
with zero contribution on strict full/empty fibers, and put
\[
R=\sum_{z\in P}\int (x-q(z))\,d\tau_z(x).
\tag{2}
\]
For the normal motion \(u(\varepsilon)=u+\varepsilon v\), with the meeting section fixed,
\[
\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\mu(H(\varepsilon))\right|_0
=v\cdot R,\qquad u\cdot R=0.
\tag{3}
\]
The coarea factor is \(1/|u|\), not the reciprocal length of the full ambient normal.

One elementary justification of (3) is to use coordinates \(x=q(z)+\xi+t\,u/|u|\). The moving cap boundary has
\[
t=-\frac{\varepsilon\,v\cdot\xi}{|u|+\varepsilon\,v\cdot u/|u|}.
\]
Fubini gives the signed swept length. Away from the boundary of the proper section, the divided swept length converges to \(v\cdot\xi/|u|\). The section boundary has zero \((d-1)\)-measure, and bounded fibers give a uniform integrable bound on this quotient. Dominated convergence proves (3). Strict full/empty traces stay fixed locally. The same formula in \(d=1\) is the proper-cut endpoint derivative with counting measure.

Taking \(v=-R\) strictly decreases this cap to first order whenever \(R\ne0\); its derivative is \(-|R|^2\). Since \(u\cdot R=0\), this is tangent to the normal sphere to first order, and positive renormalization preserves the cap. Section 1 permits these motions independently for the group.

Consequently stationarity of a positively weighted cap sum under these independent normal motions requires \(R_i=0\) for every cap with positive multiplier. A single nonzero local section displacement need not make \(R_i\ne0\); all actual fibers must be summed.

Supporting fibers with a positive \((d-1)\)-dimensional face require one-sided trace terms. They are not covered by this differentiability assertion. All simplex and star cuts below are proper, so no support coefficient or boundary force is discarded.

## 3. A lone concurrent simplex group

Let \(K\) be a \(d\)-simplex, \(d\ge2\), of volume \(V\), with barycentric coordinates \(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d\). Put \(m=d+1\). Let a group be
\[
H_i=\{\lambda_i\ge a_i\},\qquad
a_i>0,\quad \sum_i a_i=1.
\tag{4}
\]
Its meeting point \(y_a\) has barycentric coordinates \(a\). The group covers the whole affine span: its margins sum to zero.

The centroid \(g_i\) of its proper section has barycentric coordinates
\[
g_{i,i}=a_i,\qquad
g_{i,j}=\frac{1-a_i}{d}\quad(j\ne i).
\]
Write \(\delta_i=g_i-a\) in barycentric coordinates. Thus
\[
\delta_{i,i}=0,\qquad \sum_j\delta_{i,j}=0,\qquad
\delta_i\cdot a=-|\delta_i|^2.
\tag{5}
\]
The last identity follows because \(g_i\) is constant away from coordinate \(i\), so \(\delta_i\cdot g_i=0\).

The explicit fixed-meeting-point normal motion
\[
L_i(\varepsilon,x)=
\lambda_i(x)-a_i
-\varepsilon\,\delta_i\cdot(\lambda(x)-a)
\tag{6}
\]
has actual cap derivative
\[
F_i'(0)=-S_i|\delta_i|^2,\qquad
S_i=dV(1-a_i)^{d-1}.
\tag{7}
\]
Here the Euclidean norm of the displayed barycentric vector simply specifies this particular affine-normal motion. It is not asserted to equal physical Euclidean distance on an arbitrary simplex. Formula (7) also follows directly from the exact one-included-vertex cap formula, using (5). Alternatively, in physical coordinates the tangent rotation toward \(-(g_i-y_a)\) has derivative
\(-(\mathcal H^{d-1}(\text{section})/|\nabla\lambda_i|)\,|g_i-y_a|^2\).

Thus a positively weighted group stationary under every independent fixed-point normal motion must satisfy \(g_i=y_a\) at each positively weighted cap. If all \(m\) weights are positive, this forces
\[
a_0=\cdots=a_d=1/m.
\tag{8}
\]
Indeed \(\delta_i=0\) means all coordinates other than \(i\) agree; if this holds at two distinct indices, a third index exists because \(d\ge2\), and all coordinates agree.

More precisely, at a noncanonical \(a\), the stationary-index set
\(Z=\{i:\delta_i=0\}\) has at most one member. All other caps strictly decrease under (6); caps in \(Z\) stay unchanged if left fixed.

For the earlier one-high groups
\[
a_g=1-\frac{d}{3m},\qquad a_i=\frac1{3m}\quad(i\ne g),
\]
the high cap is stationary, while for each low cap
\[
\delta_{i,g}=-\frac{2(d-1)}{3d},\quad
\delta_{i,j}=\frac2{3d}\ (j\ne i,g),\quad
|\delta_i|^2=\frac{4(d-1)}{9d}>0.
\tag{9}
\]
The high cap is in fact an ordinary minimizing cap at \(y_a\): its small corner simplex realizes the own depth by the centered-inner-simplex argument. Thus it cannot be strictly decreased by a fixed-point rotation, even beyond first order. A claim of normal-only strict decrease of **every** cap of these groups would be false.

## 4. Explicit simultaneous strict decrease after allowing meeting-point motion

Every noncanonical group (4), \(d\ge2\), does admit a combined motion which strictly decreases all its cap volumes and preserves full-space cover.

If \(Z\) is empty, set \(h=0\) and \(k_i=1/|\delta_i|^2\). If \(Z\) has one member, set
\[
h_i=1\quad(i\in Z),\qquad h_i=-1/d\quad(i\notin Z),
\]
\[
k_i=0\quad(i\in Z),\qquad
k_i=\frac{1+1/d}{|\delta_i|^2}\quad(i\notin Z).
\]
In either case \(\sum_i h_i=0\). Put \(a(\varepsilon)=a+\varepsilon h\), which remains positive for sufficiently small positive \(\varepsilon\), and use the caps
\[
L_i(\varepsilon,x)=
\lambda_i(x)-a_i(\varepsilon)
-\varepsilon k_i\,\delta_i\cdot(\lambda(x)-a(\varepsilon)).
\tag{10}
\]
All boundaries meet at \(a(\varepsilon)\). Their normals stay positively spanning for small \(\varepsilon\). Their exact first derivatives are
\[
F_i'(0)=-S_i\bigl(h_i+k_i|\delta_i|^2\bigr)=-S_i<0.
\tag{11}
\]
Smoothness of the proper cap formulas makes every cap strictly smaller for all sufficiently small positive \(\varepsilon\).

There is also an explicit balance certificate. Let \(D\) have row \(k_i\delta_i\), so \(D\mathbf1=0\), and let \(R_\varepsilon=I-\varepsilon D\). If
\(\varepsilon\|D^T\|_\infty<1/3\), then
\[
\eta=R_\varepsilon^{-T}\mathbf1
\]
has all entries positive: the Neumann bound gives
\(\|\eta-\mathbf1\|_\infty<1/2\). Consequently
\[
\sum_i\eta_iL_i(\varepsilon,x)
=\mathbf1\cdot(\lambda(x)-a(\varepsilon))=0,
\]
which proves exact full-space coverage at every point, including the meeting point. This also shows directly that the perturbed group remains a positive circuit.

For the canonical group all \(\delta_i=0\). A first-order meeting motion has derivatives \(-S_i h_i\), with \(\sum_i h_i=0\), so they cannot all be negative. More strongly, any cap group covering the whole simplex has a member containing its centroid, of mass at least \(\Gamma_dV\), which is the common canonical mass. Thus simultaneous strict improvement of all canonical masses while preserving cover is impossible.

The restriction \(d\ge2\) is material. For an interval both concurrent sections are the meeting point at every threshold, and moving that point trades one cap length against the other. The noncanonical strict-improvement statement does not hold in dimension one.

These conclusions concern cap parameters of a fixed simplex. They do not contradict a negative physical Hessian obtained while all caps are held fixed. They show that the earlier noncanonical concurrent examples are not stationary when the normal freedoms in (6) are added.

## 5. Exact cancellation in the actual critical mixed star

Now use the actual compatible source from **candidate 8ac7846221e4d65a**:
\[
K_{-1}=K,\qquad K_0=B=K-K,\qquad K_1=-K,
\tag{12}
\]
where \(K\) is a centered \(d\)-simplex and \(|K|=V\), \(|B|=U\). Strict midpoint compatibility follows from
\((K+(-K))/2=B/2\subset\operatorname{int}B\).
The total mass is \(M=2V+U\), and central reflection of the whole mixed source gives exact maximum depth \(D=M/2\) at \((0,0)\).

Write \(\lambda_i(x)=l_i(x)+1/m\), and take any proper concurrent threshold vector \(a\) as in (4). Its actual caps are
\[
L_i(z,x)=l_i(x)+(a_i-1/m)z
=l_i(x+z y_a).
\tag{13}
\]
Thus their common affine meeting section is \(q(z)=-z y_a\). They cover the whole ambient space, and each has global mass \(D\).

For a fixed index \(i\), let \(\tau\) be the section coarea measure on \(K\cap\{\lambda_i=a_i\}\), of mass \(S_i\), and let \(g_i\) be its physical centroid. At base \(-1\), the contribution to (2) is
\[
R_i^- = S_i(g_i-y_a).
\]
At base \(+1\), reflection \(x=-X\) identifies its section and its coarea factor with the same section of \(K\), giving
\[
R_i^+ =-S_i(g_i-y_a).
\]
The middle section of the symmetric body \(B\) is centrally symmetric about zero, so \(R_i^0=0\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{\quad R_i^-+R_i^0+R_i^+=0\quad}
\tag{14}
\]
for every cap, regardless of how noncanonical its endpoint threshold is.

The actual full section moments satisfy the stronger identities
\[
\sum_z\int x\,d\tau_z=0,\qquad
\sum_z z\,\tau_z(K_z)=0.
\tag{15}
\]
Thus arbitrary first-order continuous-normal and base-normal variations of a cap through the fixed central point have zero global derivative. This is not merely a cancellation at one chosen meeting section.

In fact the global mass is exactly constant, not just stationary: every nonvertical hyperplane through \((0,0)\) bisects the centrally symmetric mixed measure. Hence every sufficiently small nonvertical cap-normal motion through that point has mass \(D\). In particular the cover-preserving motions
\[
\widetilde L_i(z,x)=\widetilde u_i\cdot(x+z\widetilde y_a)
\]
may rotate all continuous normals and change the group's endpoint meeting point while preserving its central contact; all global cap masses remain \(D\). Any decrease of the \(K\)-endpoint trace is paid exactly by an increase of the reflected endpoint trace, while the middle contribution remains \(U/2\).

This is an actual critical, full-dimensional, convex-compatible obstruction to replacing (14) by local section-centroid equality. Positive multipliers and even the previously computed strictly negative free-endpoint physical Hessian do not remove it.

The normal cancellation itself already occurs for a **single inclusion-minimal circuit cover**. Keep just one group (13). At base zero, take a sufficiently small positive multiple of the centered simplex vertex \(v_i\); it belongs to the interior of \(B\). Since \(l_i(v_i)=d/m>0\) and \(l_j(v_i)=-1/m<0\) for \(j\ne i\), this actual source point is covered only by cap \(i\). Every member of the group is therefore necessary for that cover. Removing the other groups does not change (14) or the exact cap-mass flatness. It does, however, remove the previously specified multigroup threshold-variance stress and its physical Hessian; those additional properties are not claimed for the reduced group.

The star's normalized depth is \(1/2\), above the relevant OC target. In the binary embedding of the cited note, sufficiently small star-cap motions retain the strict exclusion of all added fibers; their global masses therefore remain constant there too. That family approaches the OC ratio only by increasing integer dimension, uses a redundant cap family, and makes no below-target or minimal-cover claim.

The exact verifier **../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_concurrent_normal_motion_and_section_cancellation.py** checks the lone-simplex derivatives, positive circuit certificates and finite strict-decrease paths, and the reflected global section-moment cancellation. The arguments above establish the all-parameter statements independently of the finite checks.
